prompts.cooked: Use case: style-transfer. Primary request: completely redraw COOKED MEAT to belong to the same sprite family as raw meat and the approved dried meat. Input image 1: RAW MEAT is the primary cut shape and angle reference. Input image 2: approved JERKY is the preferred pixel-art, outline, scale and silhouette reference. Input image 3: OLD COOKED MEAT is the edit target and only identifies the food category; replace its overly thick wide steak shape and black barbecue stripes with the same elongated simple cut as raw meat. Asset type: one production transparent 2D inventory / held food sprite for FlatWorld, a top-down survival sandbox. Style-transfer to match the provided RAW MEAT and USER-APPROVED JERKY, with the same simple elongated boneless meat-cut identity and bottom-left to top-right diagonal. Low-saturation naturalistic retro PIXEL ART, big deliberate connected square pixel clusters, dark warm contour, a few coherent tonal steps, clear outer silhouette, upper-left illumination. Match the approved jerky's coarse pixel scale and restrained detail: approximately 40–48 logical pixels across the silhouette, rendered at full native high resolution with crisp square cluster steps. Center one single cut, leave clean transparent margin on all sides. Genuinely transparent background, preserve alpha; no baked checkerboard, no drop shadow, no scene, plate, bowl, utensils, packaging, bone, text, watermark or extra props. Do not add tiny noisy pixels, painted microtexture, smooth gradients or wet photographic shine. Keep full native output resolution. Subject: a fully cooked, gently shrunken but still plump and tender boneless piece of meat, elongated rounded irregular oval like the raw cut, a shallow visible side edge, warm chestnut and russet-brown cooked flesh, restrained golden-brown seared outer rim, a few broad lighter brown muscle lobes and short irregular cooking creases. It must visibly read as cooked flesh: warmer and lighter than the dark dry jerky, fuller and smoother in broad clusters, without the jerky's deep long dry cracks. No raw pink/red center, no bloody marbling, no bright white raw fat, no coal-black grill stripes, no crosshatch, no burnt charcoal, no wood-grain or bread appearance. Natural shallow thickness, approximately the same length-to-width silhouette as the reference raw meat and jerky. Output only ONE finished cooked meat sprite.
prompts.cured: Use case: style-transfer. Primary request: completely redraw SALT-CURED MEAT to belong to the same sprite family as raw meat and the approved dried meat. Input image 1: RAW MEAT is the primary cut shape and angle reference. Input image 2: approved JERKY is the preferred pixel-art, outline, scale and silhouette reference. Input image 3: OLD SALT-CURED MEAT is the edit target and only identifies the food category; replace its rectangular stacked bacon-block silhouette with a single elongated cut derived from raw meat. Asset type: one production transparent 2D inventory / held food sprite for FlatWorld, a top-down survival sandbox. Style-transfer to match the provided RAW MEAT and USER-APPROVED JERKY, with the same simple elongated boneless meat-cut identity and bottom-left to top-right diagonal. Low-saturation naturalistic retro PIXEL ART, big deliberate connected square pixel clusters, dark warm contour, a few coherent tonal steps, clear outer silhouette, upper-left illumination. Match the approved jerky's coarse pixel scale and restrained detail: approximately 40–48 logical pixels across the silhouette, rendered at full native high resolution with crisp square cluster steps. Center one single cut, leave clean transparent margin on all sides. Genuinely transparent background, preserve alpha; no baked checkerboard, no drop shadow, no scene, plate, bowl, utensils, packaging, bone, text, watermark or extra props. Do not add tiny noisy pixels, painted microtexture, smooth gradients or wet photographic shine. Keep full native output resolution. Subject: a single boneless salt-cured piece of meat made from this raw meat cut, an elongated rounded irregular oval, slightly tightened edges but still fleshy rather than dried flat. Muted deep rose / burgundy-red cured flesh, restrained pale ivory fat along only part of its perimeter and one simple muscle separation, a few tiny coarse ivory salt clusters embedded on the meat surface, 3–5 sparse clusters only, not floating seasoning props. The fat is sparse rather than stacked layered bacon; the salt should be legible and restrained. The cured meat is distinctly rose-red with pale salt/fat accents compared with warm brown cooked meat and dark wrinkled jerky. No black grill marks, no golden cooked crust, no burnt surface, no dark deep jerky cracks, no green spoilage, no sausage, no bread, no rectangular bacon slab or stacked meat strips. Same diagonal and shallow cut volume as raw reference. Output only ONE finished salt-cured meat sprite.
